newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Matav says mulls bidding for TV channel.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Matav says mulls bidding for TV channel.

text.p: Hungarian telecommunications company Matav Rt said on Monday it was considering bidding for one of the national TV channels to be offered this year on ten-year concessions.
"We are considering the possibility as we regard the media as a natural expansion field in our strategy," Matav general director Elek Straub told Reuters.
Hungary will shortly offer the channels for a minimum eight billion forints per channel per year concession fee.
Only consortia are expected to bid and no single company is allowed to have more than a 49 percent stake, while Hungarians have to hold a minimum of 26 percent.
Straub added that taking part in a TV tender was just one of the media involvements Matav was considering.
"We are considering several different possibilities to enter the 'content industry'" Straub said.
He added that final decisions on some of these projects could be expected this year.

Foreign companies said to be lining up to bid for the TV channels include U.S.-based Central European Media Enterprises, CLT-Bertelsmann, which owns RTL satellite television, a Hungarian-Swedish consortium MTM-SBS and a consortium of French channel TF1 and the German Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung.

Matav, Hungary's third largest company, is 67 percent owned by a 50-50 consortium of Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech Corp, while the state holds a 25 percent stake and the rest is held by a variety of investors.

Matav is expected to apply for listing on a foreign bourse probably this year, in addition to the Budapest Stock Exchange, but the company has said only that it has chosen Merrill Lynch as adviser for a possible IPO.
